name: Score automotive editorial prospects — public API — layout fixed

parameters.content:
## Score automotive backlink prospects

### How it works

1. The manual trigger loads product catalogs from the European and North American WooCommerce stores.
2. The workflow reads editorial prospects from Google Sheets and matches each eligible lead to a regional product.
3. It fetches the editorial page's title and description. Failed requests are routed to technical review before an AI call.
4. OpenAI assesses page-context relevance and suggests an editorial angle and anchor text.
5. The workflow scores the proposal and updates one review record per prospect in Google Sheets.

### Setup steps

- [ ] Verify **Fetch EU Products** returns public JSON from `https://tangmacraftsman.com/wp-json/wc/store/v1/products?per_page=100&page=1` (first 100 only).
- [ ] Verify **Fetch NA Products** returns public JSON from `https://tangmacraftsmans.com/wp-json/wc/store/v1/products?per_page=100&page=1` (NA endpoint not yet verified).
- [ ] Connect Google Sheets OAuth to all three Sheets nodes. Replace `REPLACE_WITH_SPREADSHEET_ID`, select `Pending_Leads` and `Opportunities`, and choose `opportunity_key` as the matching column in both output nodes.
- [ ] In `Pending_Leads`, add `prospect_id`, `target_url`, `target_region`, `brand`, `model`, `part_category` and `permission_status`. Region must be `EU` or `NA`; permission must be `approved` to fetch.
- [ ] Add optional input metrics: `domain_rating`, `organic_traffic`, `placement_type`, `link_attribute`. Create matching output headers before running; see the save-stage note.
- [ ] Add an OpenAI HTTP Bearer Auth credential to **Analyze Editorial Relevance**, confirm the chosen model, and test a few rows in a copied sheet.

### Customization

Adjust the product-text threshold in **Match Product to Prospect**, scoring thresholds in **Score Proposal**, or the OpenAI model and prompt. To use other stores, replace the Store API URLs and regional host checks in the matching Code node.

### Regional product sources

[Europe store — EUR](https://tangmacraftsman.com/)

[North America store — USD](https://tangmacraftsmans.com/)

The output supports human editorial review. It does not publish links, send outreach, confirm fitment or verify certification/PBN status. DR, traffic and permission are supplied sheet values.

## Load regional product catalogs

The manual trigger reads EU products and then NA products through public WooCommerce Store API HTTP requests. Published products and their regional permalinks provide the candidate pool for matching. No WooCommerce credentials are required. Product records are read, not changed.

## Validate and match prospects

Google Sheets reads the lead list. The Code node checks required fields, permission and URL rules, then picks a published regional product using brand/model/category text scores (35/35/20, minimum 55). Eligible rows take the upper branch; rejected rows take the review branch below. The match is a textual candidate, not confirmed vehicle fitment.

## Fetch usable editorial metadata

The HTTP node requests the editorial URL with a 15-second timeout and redirects disabled. The parser extracts title and Meta Description; the IF node passes usable HTML metadata to AI. Request, HTTP, non-HTML or missing-metadata failures go to the technical-review formatter below without an AI call.

## Assess and score relevance

OpenAI receives the lead topic, matched product and page metadata, and returns a 0–60 relevance score, rationale, pitch angle and suggested anchors. The Code node adds up to 40 points from supplied DR/traffic metrics. Totals of 70 or more are ready for human review; lower totals are archived. AI/API errors and paid-link questions are flagged.

## Save evaluated review records

This node upserts scored and fetch-failure records to `Opportunities`. Match on `opportunity_key` (`region|prospect_id`) so later runs update the same prospect. Use the same sheet and match column as the other output node. Prepare the output headers listed in the sheet-schema note below.

## Save rejected input records

Rows with invalid or incomplete input, pending permission or no candidate bypass fetching and AI. The formatter records validation flags and the status `Needs input or permission review`; the Sheets node upserts the record into the same `Opportunities` tab. Correct the source row and rerun it with the same prospect ID.

## Record technical fetch failures

A failed page request or unusable metadata produces a `Needs technical review` record with its fetch error in `review_flags` and an AI score of zero. It then uses the evaluated-output upsert node. Inspect the URL and response before retrying; this branch makes no AI request.

## Prepare output columns and test

Create these headers in `Opportunities` before running:

`opportunity_key`, `prospect_id`, `site`, `domain`, `target_url`, `brand`, `model`, `part_category`, `product_id`, `product_title`, `product_url`, `product_match_score`, `page_title`, `meta_description`, `domain_rating`, `organic_traffic`, `quant_score`, `ai_relevance_score`, `total_score`, `ai_rationale`, `pitch_topic`, `recommended_anchors`, `permission_status`, `link_attribute`, `review_flags`, `status`, `checked_at`.

Use **Append or Update Row** with matching column `opportunity_key` in both output nodes. Missing prospect IDs receive a stable fallback key and remain flagged. Avoid concurrent runs against the same sheet.

Input example: `P-001 | https://example.org/bmw-x5-guide | EU | BMW | X5 E70 | headlight | approved`. Replace the illustrative URL with a real editorial page.

Test EU and NA public Store API responses (NA has not yet been verified), pending permission, an unreachable page, an AI/API failure and a second run of the same ID. Review all four statuses and confirm one row per key. Credentials and sheet access must be tested in your own n8n instance.
